scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user reboots their PC and now cannot get an IP address. Other
PCs that were already up keep working (their existing leases are
still valid). Newly connected devices on any internal VLAN time
out waiting for DHCP. Existing TCP sessions are unaffected.
Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 dhcpd (ISC DHCP server)
Mechanism: r1 is the central DHCP server for every internal
  VLAN (A-PC, A-Phone, A-Mgmt, B-PC, B-Phone, B-Mgmt, Wi-Fi).
  DSWs relay DHCPDISCOVER as unicast to 10.0.0.76 (R1's
  loopback). With dhcpd dead, requests reach r1 but get no
  reply. Existing leases keep working until their lifetime
  expires; renewals start failing after lease-time/2.
Localization: r1
Root cause: dhcpd is not running on r1
Fix: restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)
scenario.fix_spec:
restart dhcpd — `/etc/init.d/isc-dhcp-server restart`
  on r1 (or however the lab launches dhcpd)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Central DHCP service (isc-dhcp-server) on the WAN/edge router r1. Distribution switches dswa1 and dswb1 are correctly running dhcrelay on all internal VLAN SVIs and forwarding requests to the DHCP server IP 10.0.0.76.

Mechanism: New clients send DHCPDISCOVERs, which the relays forward to 10.0.0.76. Because no DHCP daemon is listening on r1, no DHCPOFFERs return, so clients time out with no lease. Existing devices keep working because their leases and established TCP sessions do not require new DHCP exchanges.

Localization: 
- dswa1: dhcrelay -i br0.10 -i br0.20 -i br0.40 -i br0.99 -i eth5 -i eth6 10.0.0.76 (listening on UDP 67).
- dswb1: dhcrelay -i br0.10 -i br0.20 -i br0.30 -i br0.99 -i eth5 -i eth6 10.0.0.76 (listening on UDP 67).
- r1: isc-dhcp-server is inactive (dead) and nothing is bound to UDP/67 (only dhclient on UDP/68). r1 has 10.0.0.76/32 on lo and a valid dhcpd.conf covering all VLAN subnets.

Root cause: The ISC DHCP server process on r1 is not running, leaving the DHCP relay targets with no responder.

Corrective fix: Start and enable the DHCP server on r1: systemctl start isc-dhcp-server; systemctl enable isc-dhcp-server. Verify it listens on UDP/67 and that relays can reach 10.0.0.76. Consider adding a secondary DHCP server or configuring the relays with multiple upstreams for resilience.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies r1 as the affected device and states the isc-dhcp-server on r1 is inactive.
The agent explicitly identifies the ISC DHCP server (dhcpd/isc-dhcp-server) on r1 as the affected component and states it is not running.
The report explicitly states that existing devices keep working due to existing leases while new DHCPDISCOVERs receive no offers, correctly distinguishing existing vs new lease behavior.
Proposes starting/enabling the isc-dhcp-server on r1 (systemctl start/enable) and verifying UDP/67—matches the expected remediation to restart the DHCP daemon.

The investigation log clearly shows dhcrelay instances forwarding to 10.0.0.76, r1 has no dhcpd process and systemctl reports isc-dhcp-server inactive, and no UDP/67 listener on r1 — supporting the conclusion that the DHCP server is down. Minor missing explicit evidence of the 10.0.0.76 loopback on r1 is the only small gap.
